source.title_on_document: The Effects of Generative AI on Design Fixation and Divergent Thinking

supplement.where: "The full study protocol can be found in supplementary material." (p. 4, Section 3.1). No URL given.
supplement.holds: The full study protocol. All model results (Tables 1-4) and the NASA-TLX appendix (Table A.1, p. 18) are in this PDF.

paper_design_summary: Sixty students with visual design experience were randomly assigned, in a lab, to one of three conditions (20 each): no inspiration support, Google Image Search, or Midjourney V4. Each spent 20 minutes sketching as many ideas as possible for a chatbot avatar after seeing an example avatar meant to induce fixation. Raters scored the 277 sketches for design fixation (features copied from the example), fluency (sketch count), variety (clusters per participant), and originality (rarity of a sketch's cluster among other participants); Bayesian models compare each support condition with the no-support baseline.

studies.label: Lab experiment: chatbot avatar sketching with no support, Google Image Search, or Midjourney

assignment.what_was_assigned: Inspiration stimulus available during the sketching task: none (Baseline), Google Image Search, or Midjourney V4 (GenAI)
assignment.quote: After completing the questionnaire, the participants were randomly assigned to one of the three conditions and were assigned a unique ID generated by the computer (3 random digits)
assignment.locator: p. 6, Section 3.3 Procedure; design also p. 3, Section 3 and p. 4, Section 3.1

arms.name: GenAI
arms.description: Access to the paid version of Midjourney V4 through a private Discord server; text prompts return sets of four images; video tutorial before the task

arms.name: Image Search
arms.description: Access to Google Images in an incognito browser during the task; video tutorial before the task

arms.name: Baseline (No support)
arms.description: No inspiration support; same brief, example avatar, materials, and 20-minute limit

participants.exclusions: None reported. The paper says 60 participants were recruited and randomly assigned, and reports N=60 for the experiment (abstract) and F(2, 57) for the NASA-TLX ANOVA (p. 6). Per-arm counts (20 each) come from "Each condition had an equal number of participants and was gender-balanced, with 10 women and 10 men per condition" (p. 5); the paper does not say how gender balance was achieved under random assignment. The 60 participants produced 277 sketches (p. 5).
participants.who: Undergraduate, master's and PhD students from arts, business, computer science and IT, design, engineering, and science, aged 18 or older with self-described visual design experience; mean age 25.8 (18-49, SD 5.4); few had professional industry experience (p. 16, Section 5.4).
participants.country: not stated; recruited through university student notice boards and clubs; authors at The University of Melbourne and RMIT, Melbourne, Australia
participants.quote: We recruited 60 participants through digital student notice boards, mailing lists of university student clubs, and word of mouth.

ai_tool.name_model: Midjourney V4 (paid version, default model in May 2023), via a private Discord server
ai_tool.how_used: Participants entered text prompts and viewed sets of four generated images as inspiration while sketching on paper. GenAI participants wrote 117 prompts in total (mean 5.85 per participant, range 2-15), and Midjourney returned 468 images (pp. 11-12).

task.description: Sketch on paper as many ideas as possible for a chatbot avatar (kind, loving, caring, intelligent); the brief included an example robot avatar with 14 salient features to induce design fixation.
task.duration: 20 minutes for the design task; sessions 45-60 minutes in total

outcomes.name: Originality
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Two raters blind to condition grouped all 277 sketches into 83 clusters. A sketch's originality = 1 - (number of other participants with an idea in the same cluster / number of other participants) (Eq. 4, p. 5). Linear regression with participant random effect; total-effects model (Stimulus only) and direct-effects model (adds Variety). Figure 9 plots the score averaged per participant.

contrasts.reported: Table 4 (Bayesian linear model, posterior mean (SD), 89% CI): Total effects GenAI -.03 (.02) [-.06, -.01], Intercept .86 (.01) [.84, .88]; Direct effects GenAI -.03 (0.02) [-.05, -.01]. Text: "97% probability of being negative (mean = -.03, 89% CI [-.06, .00]), and a Bayes Factor of 35." The paper calls the effects "negligible".

No direct GenAI vs Image Search estimate printed. Figure 9 posterior predictions (median and SE) place GenAI below Image Search (approx. 0.83 vs 0.85, read from the figure). Table 4 Image Search total effect vs baseline: -.01 (.02) [-.04, .01].

outcomes.name: Variety
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Number of the 83 rater-defined clusters that a participant's sketches fall into, minus 1 (Eq. 3 normalizes by 83 - 1 for plots). Negative binomial model with log link on the count; total effects (Stimulus) and direct effects (adds Fluency).

contrasts.reported: Table 3 (negative binomial, log link, posterior mean (SD), 89% CI): Total effects GenAI -.29 (-.28) [-.74, .17] (SD printed as negative), Intercept 1.01 (.19) [.71, 1.30]; Direct effects GenAI -.15 (0.24) [-.53, .23]. Text: total "86% probability of being negative (mean = -.29, 89% CI [-.75, .16]), and a Bayes Factor of 5.93"; direct "mean = -.15 [-55, .24]", Bayes Factor 2.64. The 89% interval includes zero.
contrasts.locator: p. 9, Table 3 and Section 4.4; p. 10 text; Figure 8

contrasts.reported: No direct estimate printed. Figure 8 posterior predictions place GenAI above Image Search (approx. 0.060 vs 0.054 share of clusters, read from the figure). Table 3 Image Search total effect vs baseline: -.39 (.28) [-.84, -.06].

outcomes.name: Fluency
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Number of sketches a participant produced in 20 minutes (Eq. 2). Negative binomial model with log link; total effects (Stimulus) and direct effects (adds offset(log(Time on Task))).

contrasts.reported: Table 2 (negative binomial, log link, posterior mean (SD), 89% CI): Total effects GenAI -.21 (.30) [-.66, .26], Intercept 1.50 (.19) [1.20, 1.80]; Direct effects GenAI .10 (.31) [-.39, .58]. Text: total "-.21 (89% CI [-.7, .28]) and a Bayes factor of 3.20, suggesting a 76% posterior probability of a negative effect"; direct "mean = .10, 89% CI [-.41, .60]", Bayes factor .61. The 89% interval includes zero.
contrasts.locator: p. 9, Table 2, Section 4.3 and Figure 7; p. 8 text

contrasts.reported: No direct estimate printed. Figure 7 posterior predictions place GenAI above Image Search (approx. 3.6 vs 2.7 sketches, read from the figure). Table 2 Image Search total effect vs baseline: -.49 (.25) [-.88, -.10].

outcomes.name: Design fixation score
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Two raters blind to the study aims (HCI researchers with experience teaching and evaluating design, p. 7) counted which of the 14 salient features of the example avatar appear in each sketch; DFS = features repeated / 14 (Eq. 1). Higher means more copying of the example, i.e. worse. Binomial model with probit link and random effects for participant and image.

contrasts.reported: Table 1 (binomial probit, posterior mean (SD), 89% CI): GenAI .32 (0.13) [.11, .54]; Image Search .27 (0.14) [.05, .48]; Intercept -.71 (.10) [-.86, .56] (as printed). Text: "100% probability of leading to higher Design Fixation (mean = .32, 89% CI [.11, .55]), and a Bayes Factor of 124". Higher = more fixation (worse).

No direct estimate printed. Text: "GenAI led to even more design fixation than Image Search". Figure 6 posterior predictions place GenAI slightly above Image Search (approx. 0.35 vs 0.33, read from the figure).

company_involvement.description: No company involvement stated. Midjourney and Google Images were used as off-the-shelf tools. Funding: Rowden White Scholarship and Melbourne Research Scholarship (University of Melbourne).

eligibility.reason: Participants were randomly assigned to Midjourney, Google Image Search, or no support (p. 6). Sixty people across the three arms (p. 5); the count is close to the threshold, and the GenAI vs no-support contrast has 40 people (20 per arm). Originality, variety, fluency, and design fixation are scored by raters on the sketches produced with the tool available (pp. 5, 8-10).

one_line_finding: With Midjourney available, 20 students produced sketches with lower rated originality than 20 with no support (total effect -.03, SD .02, 89% CI [-.06, -.01], Table 4, p. 10) and higher fixation on the example (.32, 89% CI [.11, .54], Table 1, p. 8), while effects on fluency and variety were negative with 89% intervals that include zero (Tables 2-3, p. 9).
open_questions: Originality is a rarity score defined relative to other participants' ideas (share of other participants with an idea in the same cluster). Under the codebook it is novelty of a single output (with_ai), but de Rooij and Biskjaer (2026) reportedly coded this paper as group-level homogenization. Review should confirm whether any outcome here should count as across_people.
The paper reports only model coefficients relative to the baseline; no GenAI vs Image Search estimate is printed, and arm means appear only as posterior predictions in Figures 6-9.

Statistics are Bayesian posterior means, posterior SDs, and 89% credible intervals, not frequentist SEs or 95% CIs. Originality and design fixation models are at the sketch level with participant random effects; fluency and variety are at the participant level.
How 10 women and 10 men per condition (p. 5) was achieved under random assignment is not stated.
notes: Several text and table numbers differ slightly: design fixation GenAI CI [.11, .55] in text vs [.11, .54] in Table 1; Table 1 intercept CI printed as [-.86, .56]; fluency total GenAI CI [-.7, .28] in text vs [-.66, .26] in Table 2; variety total GenAI SD printed as (-.28) and CI [-.75, .16] in text vs [-.74, .17] in Table 3; originality GenAI CI [-.06, .00] in text vs [-.06, -.01] in Table 4. Figure 6 caption describes scores as percentages, while the axis shows proportions. Within the GenAI arm only, the paper reports Spearman rho = 0.56 between the DFS of 82 sketches and the DFS of the AI images seen just before each sketch (p. 12, Figure 10); this is not an arm contrast and is not listed as an outcome. NASA-TLX workload (self-report) did not differ by condition, F(2, 57) = 1, p = 0.37 (p. 6; Table A.1, p. 18). Models use raw counts, and Figures 6-9 plot normalized values (p. 8, Section 4.1).
